h1: Provider Connector Shared API Interaction Contract
p: Summary · Logical contract · Sequences and reuse
These proposed requirements apply to selected capabilities, not to every possible platform function. Owning-feature rules remain authoritative; this table defines the provider connector handoff.

tr.th: Required result and safe next action

tr.td: CA-01 Feature requests an operation
Check caller, represented business, environment, role and qualified capability before execution. Deny unsupported or unauthorised combinations without an external call.
Wrong tenant, expired authority, wrong environment and unsupported operation produce no external effect.
CA-02 Feature requests an external mutation
Preserve operation identity, fixed input and original execution context. Repetition with the same identity/input follows the approved duplicate contract; changed input conflicts.
Concurrent duplicates produce one authorised execution owner; key reuse with changed payload is rejected.
CA-03 Platform returns a response or the call times out
Preserve source code, correlation and protected evidence. Return the actual known result or an unknown outcome. Reconcile a possible external effect before retry or reassignment.
Lost response after external acceptance does not cause blind resend or automatic platform failover.
CA-04 Platform supplies an invoice or event
Authenticate the source and hand off durable content/evidence to its feature owner. Advance acquisition progress only after the agreed durable handoff.
Duplicate notification or failed handoff causes no lost invoice and no duplicate business processing.
CA-05 Connection, credential or contract changes
Apply approved changes to future work. Retain original context for pending actions; revoked authority can block further external access.
Pending work is not silently rebound to another provider, role, environment or customer.

h2: 2 Shared API usage and execution context
p: Products, authorised providers and Provider Connectors use the same Sage API contract under 044 CA-ARCH01/02. This section defines logical information needed for those interactions; it does not define another Connector API. Reuse actual shared-API fields and operations. SPEC013 GPA-Q02/Q05 still govern exact wire schemas, versions and duplicate handling.

tr.td: Product → Sage
Request setup or invoice work; read permitted saved results. Use the customer's scope and operation identity.
Authorised provider → Sage
Submit or retrieve assigned invoices/results under the selected provider integration mode. Partner status alone does not grant all product or connector permissions.
Provider Connector → Sage
Use the common contract to obtain permitted work/content and submit source invoices, statuses or execution evidence. Work may arrive through notifications.
Provider Connector → external platform
Use that platform's separate external contract. Do not forward caller input to arbitrary endpoints.

p: Caller permissions, tenant isolation and one executor per exchange action remain CA-01–05 / SPEC013 controls. Consumer-role isolation must be tested as part of CS02; sharing an API does not grant interchangeable permissions.

tr.td: Accepted work / execution context

Feature operation ID; exchange-action ID where applicable; authenticated-caller reference; tenant and represented-business reference; country/environment; integration role; connection and contract-profile version; capability/operation; input reference and digest; correlation; protected credential reference.
Result submitted through shared API

Original operation/action and platform context; attempt identity; source request/reference; observed time; known/pending/unknown/denied-or-unsupported classification; raw source code and protected evidence reference; recovery responsibility and permitted next action. Classifications are logical, not new wire enums.
Source invoice/event submitted through shared API

Authenticated platform/account context; stable source event/document identity where available; original bytes or protected reference and digest; source and observed timestamps; continuation/checkpoint context where applicable.

p: The owning feature determines payload readiness and business meaning. The provider connector applies the approved transport envelope and preserves external responses. DTS remains the preferred transformation candidate upstream; provider connector transport does not introduce a parallel invoice mapper, route engine or invoice store.

Record support per platform, role, environment and contract version. Use qualified, contract evidence only, unknown or excluded; no provider connector-wide ready flag may imply all functions are supported.

tr.td: Setup/access check
Account linking, token exchange or registration only where the provider contract requires it. Unknown for the complete six-provider set.
Qualify credentials and access for each operation. No external enrolment API is established by the supplied baseline. CA-SPFE; onboarding 038–040.
Send
Qualify submission, acknowledgements, duplicate behaviour and query/recovery.
SendInvoice; CA-SPFE / SPFE-S16. Feature owns delivery/public-copy meaning.
Receive/query/download
Qualify polling or push, pagination, capture and replay.
GetRegisteredInvoice, GetInvoices, DownloadInvoicesByID, DownloadInvoicesByLOC; SPFE-S12–S15.
Lifecycle/event reporting
Qualify source codes, event direction and reporting/query operations separately.
CustomerInvoiceEvents, SupplierInvoiceEvents; SPFE-S11/S17. Lifecycle owns interpretation.
Cancellation/exit
Qualify cancellation and disconnection independently.
CancelInvoice is not proof of customer offboarding or deletion; SPFE-S10.
PRE validation
Include only if supported and selected.
ValidationInvoice, direct SOAP rather than ebMS/MIME; SPFE-S23. Missing imported business schemas remain open.

p: This is the authoritative provider connector scenario list. CA-01–05 define shared controls; the checks below apply them to observable cases. Feature-specific invoice, onboarding and lifecycle scenarios stay in their owning folders. These are acceptance checks to execute, not passed test results.

tr.th: Expected evidence and safe next action

tr.td: CS01 Setup: existing private-provider customer, new private-provider customer or public access check

Existing private customer: link the existing provider account, verify Sage access and reuse valid setup; do not create a duplicate account or repeat completed registration. New private customer: support the provider-required account setup/registration and authorisation, including an external handoff where required; return pending actions until readiness is established. Test both paths for each of the six private providers. Return setup evidence to onboarding; neither path silently activates a route. SPFE: check operation access without inventing enrolment.
CA-01/02; operation A/B; onboarding ONB-S01/S03; CA-SPFE
CS02 Wrong scope, missing authority or unsupported capability/version

No external call; reason and responsible owner returned. Check wrong tenant, business, country, environment and customer-provider versus peer role separately. Test product, provider and connector caller permissions independently against the shared contract.
CA-01; operation A
CS03 Duplicate/concurrent request or identity reused with changed payload
Same identity/input correlates to the original operation; changed input conflicts. Test concurrent claims and worker restart before sending.
CA-02; operation A
CS04 Known external acceptance
Evidence and original action references persist; feature receives only the result proved by that acknowledgement. Technical acceptance does not become buyer acceptance.
CA-02/03; operation B
CS05 Platform rejection, malformed response or transport fault
Original fault/evidence retained with its level. A parser failure cannot be reported as invoice rejection; possible effects remain uncertain.
CA-03; operation B/C; SPEC011 public fault checks
CS06 Timeout or lost response after possible external acceptance
No blind resend. Qualified query reconciles the original identity; unsupported query or unresolved result holds work for its recovery owner.
CA-03; operation C
CS07 Save/worker failure before call or after response
Failed intent save prevents sending. Crash after external call or failed evidence save recovers the original attempt; no fresh mutation just to rebuild local evidence.
CA-02/03; operation A/C
CS08 Poll returns pages, empty result, duplicate item or expired cursor
Covered progress follows durable capture. Empty result is separate from outage; gaps/expired cursors require qualified rescan or owner action before claiming complete coverage.
CA-04; acquisition A–C
CS09 Valid, unauthenticated or replayed push
Check source/account scope and replay identity before handoff. Invalid source rejected; valid repeat cannot create duplicate business processing. SPFE push remains unqualified.
CA-01/04; acquisition A/C
CS10 Failure between inbound capture and acknowledgement/checkpoint
Restart replays the same saved item; committed capture deduplicates it. External acknowledgement follows the selected platform contract without losing captured work.
CA-04; acquisition B/C
CS11 Credential expiry, rotation or authority revocation during work
New external calls recheck effective permission. Rotation cannot change represented business/environment; blocked pending work retains its history and recovery owner.
CA-01/05; operation A/C
CS12 Route/provider/profile change with pending actions
New work uses only the approved new context. Earlier actions retain original context; unknown effects cannot trigger automatic failover or an alternative executor.
CA-03/05; operation C; SPEC014
CS13 Batch partial result or delivery succeeds while public-copy/reporting fails
Per-item and per-action evidence remain independent. Recover only unresolved work under its original identity; a batch receipt is not whole-batch external success.
CA-02/03; operation B/C; sending/lifecycle owners
CS14 Wrong country rule pack, payload profile or unqualified mapping
Reject or hold before sending; country-rule isolation and DTS mapping qualification have recorded results for the selected profile.
CA-01; operation A; SPEC008/014
CS15 Late or out-of-order response/event after recovery
Correlate to the original attempt/action; retain source and observation times. Stale evidence cannot overwrite newer execution ownership or directly regress lifecycle meaning.
CA-03/04; operation C, acquisition C; lifecycle owner
CS16 Rate limit, outage, payload limit or contract upgrade
Enforce qualified limits and backpressure. Retry timing does not override unknown-outcome checks; changed schema/version stays disabled until compatibility and recovery evidence pass.
CA-01/03/05; operation A/C; SPEC013 GPA-Q09/Q12

p: For each enabled binding, record case ID, operation/role/environment/contract version, build, source contract, result and evidence link. Mark cases applicable, excluded with reason or blocked by evidence before execution. Vary the feature operation across setup, send, acquisition, lifecycle and exit where selected. Add provider-specific cases from its error, paging, duplicate and trust contracts; the shared list alone cannot prove exhaustive platform coverage.

CA-01–05 and the logical message fields are proposed Sage controls, derived from SPEC013, GPA-Q03–06/Q10, and SPEC014, SPC-01–08. They are not external legal requirements. CA-H01 and CA-SPFE are defined with source limits in 044 REF.

tr.td: SPFE-S12–S15 / PRE 23 November 2026
DownloadInvoicesByID, DownloadInvoicesByLOC, GetInvoices, GetRegisteredInvoice, each portType/operation, documentation, binding, service
Query/download operations and transport; not complete filters, continuation rules or tested runtime coverage.
SPFE-S10/S11/S17 / same release
CancelInvoice, CustomerInvoiceEvents, SupplierInvoiceEvents, same elements
Named cancellation/event operations; not business state interpretation, offboarding or replay guarantees.

p: Transport detail remains authoritative in SPEC011, SPFE source contract binding. Acceptance of a selected SPFE capability must include its cited contract checks; passing CA-01–05 alone cannot qualify it.
